subjectUsefulness.judgment: Useful for careful, qualified understanding of this controlled correction sequence and selection of a precise follow-up target; cumbersome to scan and incomplete as a demonstration of dependent reassessment or conflict resolution.
reasons: The evaluator accurately recovers independent multi-label behavior and distinguishes scripted historical mistakes from the hosted correction.
Stable references, the explicit correction mapping, replacement-owned composition, and exact historical inspection make the account change traceable.
Direct and transitive cause labels expose unresolved dependent accounts without implying automatic error or repair.
The evaluator notices the clarification's semantic shift and selects it for further examination rather than treating acceptance as validation.
Repeated metadata and partial excerpts create a credible scanning burden, while inspection references provide a recovery path.
limitations: Only the supplied assessor input was consulted; this is not an implementation review.
The tiny numeric fixture and injected early accounts cannot establish natural error frequency, broad interpretive quality, unbiased detection, or semantic reliance.
Shared preparer/orchestrator authorship and OpenAI-family overlap limit independence; the exact preparer model is unavailable.
No actual callers, runtime observations, non-number input behavior, or consumer policy requirements are established.
The dependent examination failed evidence validation and no accepted replacement of the first-element-completeness account is supplied; the later clarification does not clear the earlier warning.
No competing root replacements are displayed in this sequence, so the separate conflict fixture must not be treated as an observed result here.

No generation error repeated as endorsed truth, established evaluator presentation misunderstanding, material evaluator omission, or unsupported evaluator extrapolation was identified within this bounded comparison. Potential presentation risks and reference limits are reported separately.
